en.value: To reduce a matrix into row echelon form, apply

english.explanation: Let A be an m × n matrix. If A is a zero matrix then A is in row-echelon form. If not then • Determine the leftmost non-zero column. • Use elementary row operations to put a 1 in the topmost position, pivot position, of this column. • Use elementary row operations to put zeros (strictly) below the pivot position. • If there are no more non-zero rows (strictly) below the pivot position, then the resulting matrix is in row- echelon form. • If not apply described steps above to the sub matrix consisting of the rows that lie (strictly below) the pivot position. • The resulting matrix is in row-echelon form.
